8.0.0.en: 1 And the word of the LORD of hosts came, saying, 2 "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; I was jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and I was jealous for her with great fury. 3 Thus saith the LORD; I am returned unto Zion, and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and Jerusalem shall be called a city of truth; and the mountain of the LORD of hosts the holy mountain.

8.0.1.en: While they were asking about the fast that they had imposed on themselves because of the captivity, He brings them into its depths so that they may discover the blazing flame of His love toward them. It is as though He answers their question by saying: I am a jealous God who loves you; touch My fiery love so that you too may become a blazing fire that events cannot extinguish.

8.1.0.en: The heavenly Bridegroom declares His jealousy for His people who have returned from the captivity, who had fallen under chastening because of their spiritual adultery and their deviation: "I was jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and I was jealous for her with great fury... I am returned unto Zion, and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and Jerusalem shall be called a city of truth; and the mountain of the LORD of hosts the holy mountain" [3].

8.1.1.en: First: God affirms His jealousy for her even though He chastened her for a time. As St. Didymus the Blind says: [This is what our Lord, the Almighty, says: "I loved Jerusalem or Zion, for I remember her after I had rejected her and cast her out so that she became despised by strangers; I love her not with just any love, but I love her with great intensity."

8.1.2.en: He is the jealous Bridegroom who longs for the return of His bride to the house of marriage. Truly His bride despised Him, committed fornication behind Him and betrayed Him (Jer 3:2); but when she came under affliction she realized her error and said: "I will go and return to my first husband; for then was it better with me than now" (Hos 2:7). The wonder is that her first husband does not reject her but rebukes her for the past, yet in His love He humbles Himself, saying: "I am returned unto Zion, and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem"... declaring His longing to dwell in her. In place of the ruin that came upon her He makes her a city of truth, and in place of the decline to which she had fallen He makes her His holy mountain].

8.1.3.en: St. Didymus the Blind says: [She is called anew a city of truth. Truth will no longer be a wilderness (a ruin) but a city crowded with inhabitants and with many buildings: the temple and the lofty houses, and streets and roads will be set up in it... From the spiritual side, Jerusalem represents the soul that contemplates the unseen and eternal things (for Jerusalem means vision of peace), so the soul sees peace through the mutual agreement between the virtuous life and divine love; for her part she is set aflame with the torch of love and returns to Him, and for His part He returns to her, hears her supplications and gives her what she asks, so she does not cease praying to Him... And she is called "a city of truth" because she walks according to the truth that she discovers under the shadow of the Law, and because she "searches the divine Scriptures" (Jn 5:39; 2 Tim 3:16) and so enjoys the truth].

8.1.4.en: This is the work of the jealous Bridegroom: He enters our heart and makes it Jerusalem, the city of truth, so that we enjoy the vision of peace between our souls and God, and enter into the depths of the evangelical truth and do not stop at the shadows and types of the Law.

8.1.5.en: He also raises us up as "His holy mountain," and as the Psalm says: "They that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion" (Ps 124:1). He lifts us up after the decline that befell us so that by His Holy Spirit we may reach the heights, firm in Him like the mountain, so that the storms of the world and the deceptions of the devil cannot shake us.

8.2.s.en: 2. The indwelling of blessing and peace:

8.2.0.en: 4 "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; There shall yet old men and old women dwell in the streets of Jerusalem, and every man with his staff in his hand for very age. 5 And the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing in the streets thereof. 6 Thus saith the LORD of hosts; If it be marvellous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in these days, should it also be marvellous in mine eyes? saith the LORD of hosts. 7 Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country; 8 And I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness. 9 Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Let your hands be strong, ye that hear in these days these words by the mouth of the prophets, which were in the day that the foundation of the house of the LORD of hosts was laid, that the temple might be built. 10 For before these days there was no hire for man, nor any hire for beast; neither was there any peace to him that went out or came in because of the affliction: for I set all men every one against his neighbour. 11 But now I will not be unto the residue of this people as in the former days, saith the LORD of hosts. 12 For the seed shall be prosperous; the vine shall give her fruit, and the ground shall give her increase, and the heavens shall give their dew; and I will cause the remnant of this people to possess all these things. 13 And it shall come to pass, that as ye were a curse among the heathen, O house of Judah, and house of Israel; so will I save you, and ye shall be a blessing: fear not, but let your hands be strong. 14 For thus saith the LORD of hosts; As I thought to punish you, when your fathers provoked me to wrath, saith the LORD of hosts, and I repented not: 15 So again have I thought in these days to do well unto Jerusalem and to the house of Judah: fear ye not.

8.2.1.en: It is as though God says to His people: Now there is something more important than asking whether you are to fast or to stop the fast of the captivity, namely, realizing your new position after I have established you as the new Jerusalem, the city of truth, and the new mount Zion, My holy mountain... Contemplate My gifts and My grace and hold fast to them. Whether you fast mourning or keep feast rejoicing, let this be your aim in you: that I dwell in you, so that My blessing rests upon you and you enjoy My surpassing peace.

8.2.2.en: Thus God reveals the blessings of His dwelling in us, saying:

8.2.3.en: First: "There shall yet old men and old women dwell in the streets of Jerusalem, and every man with his staff in his hand for very age" [4]. From the literal side, when God dwells in their midst they are filled with good days and peace dwells in them; death does not surprise them in their youth, but they live to old age, full of health, as they go down to the marketplaces of the city to buy what they need, each holding his staff in his hand. From the symbolic side, the marketplaces of Jerusalem in which the elders, men and women, sit are the overflow of wisdom that flows like a river that makes glad the city of God (Ps 46:4); all can go down to it to drink from it, or enter the marketplaces to acquire it. As the wise man says: "Wisdom crieth without; she uttereth her voice in the streets" (Prov 1:20). This wisdom is "the Person of the Lord Christ," who came down from heaven and presented Himself to us as a servant; all can acquire Him within and enjoy Him; He of whom the bride says: "By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not. I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth" (Song 3:1-2). As her heart burns with longing for her Bridegroom, she seeks "Wisdom Himself" and does not find Him beside her, so she rises through repentance from her bed and enters the Church, "the holy city," and goes about in its marketplaces and streets, and finds Him revealed within it, offering Himself to whoever seeks Him.

8.3.0.en: Second: "And the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing in the streets thereof" [5]. The presence of boys and girls also in the marketplaces, playing, indicates the tranquility that prevailed over all and the absence of war that takes joy away from old and young. As Isaiah the prophet described the messianic age: "And I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and joy in my people: and the voice of weeping shall be no more heard in her, nor the voice of crying. There shall be no more thence an infant of days, nor an old man that hath not filled his days: for the child shall die an hundred years old" (Isa 65:19-20).

8.3.1.en: Along with the elders there are also children playing in the marketplaces; these are the company of the simple who have attained to "childhood" so as to live in the Lord without care, as if the marketplaces of the Church include the wisdom of the elders together with the simplicity of children, as the Lord said to His disciples: "Be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves" (Mt 10:16). And as St. Jerome says: [Be simple as a dove so that you set a snare for no one, and be wise (skilful) as a serpent so that you allow no one to set a snare before you].

8.3.2.en: St. Didymus the Blind offers us a wonderful interpretation of these simple children who play in the marketplaces of the Church, that is, the holy city: [There are also little girls and boys who have begun to play a game worthy of praise, which David played, the man whose heart was according to the Lord (Acts 13:22; 1 Sam 13:14), fulfilling the will of Him who chose him, declaring with sure confidence: "I played before the LORD" (2 Sam 6:21). We can say that the children who play in the public places (the marketplaces) of the glorious city of the Lord are people who were consecrated to the Lord from their childhood, so that with purity and deep dignity they have been joined to holy speech that is blameless (Tit 2:7-8)].

8.3.3.en: In our commentary on the Book of Exodus we saw that the boys signify the soul and the girls the body; so when a person is sanctified in his entirety he brings forth fruits for the soul and the body together. There is no longer conflict between them, but they work together by the Holy Spirit, and the fruits come as boys and girls playing together in the marketplaces of the holy city with a glorious joy that cannot be uttered.

8.3.4.en: Finally, the marketplaces of the city have included the elders together with the old women, and the boys with the girls, that is, men with women, and the old with the young... As St. Didymus the Blind says: [All have become one choir singing one hymn with one heart, as it is written in the Psalm: "Both young men, and maidens; old men, and children: let them praise the name of the LORD" (Ps 148:12-13). As she cares for the wise elders, she does not neglect the wise old women who play their role in the Church. And as the Church rejoices in the wisdom of the elders, she is also glad in the victory of the young men, for the Apostle says: "I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one" (1 Jn 2:12-14)].

8.3.5.en: This divine work in the life of all members of the Church seems impossible, for the prophet says: "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; If it be marvellous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in these days, should it also be marvellous in mine eyes? saith the LORD of hosts?!" [6]. If the enemy had utterly destroyed Jerusalem, so that in the eyes of all it was impossible for joy to return to her, yet not in God's eyes, for "with God all things are possible" (Mt 19:26)... He restores to her her glory and her joy by His dwelling in her!

8.4.0.en: Third: "Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country; and I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness" [7-8].

8.4.1.en: The new Jerusalem does not include one choir of elders and old women and boys and girls, but one people of the Lord from the rising of the sun and its setting, for the door of salvation opens to all the nations and all become one in the Lord. This is the great blessing of God's dwelling among men and His abiding among us. St. Didymus the Blind says: [Thus saith the LORD of hosts: Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country, not only the people of the circumcision but the people from all the nations who believe in the Lord who is proclaimed in the Gospel. In ancient times the people in truth were of one nation, of the Hebrews... according to the testimony of Moses: "When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. For the LORD's portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance" (Deut 32:8-9)... As it was said: "And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious" (Isa 11:10; Rom 15:12)... "Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people" (Deut 32:43). So this people is no longer the people of the Hebrews alone, but with them are those who worship the Lord and serve Him, as the Psalm prophesied: "All nations shall serve him" (Ps 72:11), and in another text: "All nations whom thou hast made shall come and worship before thee, O Lord; and shall glorify thy name" (Ps 86:9), and also: "All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto the LORD: and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee. For the kingdom is the LORD's: and he is the governor among the nations" (Ps 22:27-28)... And the Gospel proclaims the union of men from every country by recording the words of the Savior: "Many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob" (Mt 8:11). This call is addressed to all parts of the world. To this may be added what was said: "The God of gods, the LORD, hath spoken, and called the earth from the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof" (Ps 50:1)... When did the God of gods speak and call the earth from the east to the west? When He left the people of the circumcision because they denied the Savior, the King of kings, by saying: "We have no king but Caesar" (Jn 19:15), "His blood be on us, and on our children" (Mt 27:25). So by their crucifying the Lord Christ they fell and the worship of the letter came to an end, and the Lord was able to say to them: "I have no pleasure in you, saith the LORD of hosts, neither will I accept an offering at your hand. For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen" (Mal 1:10-11)...].

8.4.2.en: Thus God restores humanity from the east and the west to be a people for Him in truth and righteousness. And what we say about humanity we say about the individual: God restores him from every blow on the right (from the east) and every blow on the left (from the west), that is, from falling under open sins and from self-righteousness, so that he may belong wholly to God, enjoying truth and righteousness in Christ Jesus.

8.5.0.en: Fourth: As the people of God gather from all the nations with one heart, it has the strengthened, strong hands that are able through the Lord to build the temple: "Let your hands be strong, ye that hear in these days these words by the mouth of the prophets, which were in the day that the foundation of the house of the LORD of hosts was laid, that the temple might be built" [9]. St. Didymus the Blind says: [The Lord Almighty commands that the hands consecrated to Him be strong... by translating the spiritual teachings into real work, so that work is joined to word; so that the hearers of the Law are not mere hearers, but turn hearing into fruit in their works].

8.5.1.en: If we have heard from the mouths of the prophets about the founding of the house of the LORD of hosts, that is, about the divine Incarnation, for the Lord Himself calls His body a temple, then this Incarnation gives strength to our hands to work by it, so that the divine commandment is transformed in our lives into a practical life lived out. God raised up this body, as it is said: "Wisdom hath builded her house" (Prov 9:1), so that God became dwelling in our midst and gives us His heavenly resources to work for the sake of His Kingdom. And as St. Didymus the Blind says: [How should the hands of those who hear the words of the prophets not be strong, when there was born of the Virgin the One who is fit to be called "God with us" (Isa 7:14)?! In truth, when God is with us our hands are strong and we can sing with a joyful voice: "The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge" (Ps 45:11-12)... He gives us a strength that transcends nature!].

8.5.2.en: Therefore let our hands be strengthened for work, and let the words of God in us be turned into life, since the Word built Himself a house by His Incarnation, giving us power to work. He has also made of us holy living stones for the building of His holy temple, for He says: "If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we (I and my Father) will come unto him, and make our abode with him" (Jn 14:23). He makes us ourselves a dwelling for Him, or a holy temple upon which the cornerstone stands, as the Apostle says: "And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone..." (Eph 2:20)].

8.6.0.en: Fifth: Our meeting with the incarnate God, and His dwelling in our midst, did not only strengthen the hands with His divine resources working in us, but also cut off the spirit of despair within us and set our depths aflame with hope. For work needs not only strong hands and striving and perseverance but also a spirit full of hope in the Lord; therefore He says: "For before these days there was no hire for man, nor any hire for beast; neither was there any peace to him that went out or came in because of the affliction: for I set all men every one against his neighbour" [10]. Affliction surrounded them (Hag 1:6, 9, 11; 2:16-19), which made man like the beast, without value, so that even if the two did something it was without profit and they did not deserve a wage! Jerusalem was desolate like a wilderness and ruled by strangers, so every effort a man made availed nothing. The toil of man, like that of the beast, in his going in or coming out became without profit, which turned their life into hell, so each one went out resisting his brother for no cause; in other words, instead of each working with his brother for the building of the house of God, each felt humiliation, total loss and inner emptiness, and so turned to resisting his brothers and troubling them.

8.6.1.en: From the spiritual side, a person without his meeting with his Savior, who established His holy temple, is like the beast: he works without understanding or wisdom, and so does not deserve a wage. St. Didymus the Blind says: [Scripture rebukes those who are without mind, who are in folly, saying: "Be ye not as the horse, or as the mule, which have no understanding" (Ps 83:9). Truly, how can there be a wage for people who do everything without understanding or reason?!].

8.7.0.en: This is a bitter picture of humanity apart from the work of God: it goes out to work and comes in to reckoning and finds itself in emptiness, without fruit, and not deserving reward, since each one is occupied with resisting his brother, as the Psalm says: "They speak vanity every one with his neighbour: with flattering lips" (Ps 12:3), and as was said by Jeremiah the prophet: "Every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders. And they will deceive every one his neighbour, and will not speak the truth: they have taught their tongue to speak lies, and weary themselves to commit iniquity" (Jer 9:4-5). But under the New Covenant Jerusalem stands on true peace and brings increasing fruits, so the toil of man and beast is no longer without wage as it was formerly. He says: "But now I will not be unto the residue of this people as in the former days, saith the LORD of hosts. But the seed of peace; the vine shall give her fruit, and the ground shall give her increase, and the heavens shall give their dew; and I will cause the remnant of this people to possess all these things: [11-12]. What a joyful picture after man was working without reason like the beast, so that he had no wage, as the soul (man) loses its fruit as the body (the beast) loses its sanctity, and each resists the other; now that the Lord dwells in him, not only does his soul enjoy the wage but his body also, and there is spiritual accord between them and he has surpassing spiritual fruit, and the earth works on his behalf as heaven does, in the Lord. As the Lord returns to him and dwells within him and establishes His kingdom in his heart, the seed of peace appears, which the Father Himself plants by His Holy Spirit, and the fruits of the Holy Spirit appear as the fruits of the true vine, and the earth (the body) gives its increase as the body bears a special sanctity and becomes instruments of righteousness for God, and heaven (the soul) gives its dew, as the grace of the Holy Spirit fills it... All these God gives to the soul that receives Him in it.

8.7.1.en: St. Didymus the Blind says: [This glorious reform was fulfilled in the spiritual sense when He came who said: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised" (Lk 4:18)... It is written: "In his days shall the righteous shine forth, and abundance of peace; his peace shall know no barriers; it shall not be for one nation but for the company of the nations." The whole earth that is subject to Him who said to His disciples and to those who desire to serve Him: "My peace I give unto you" (Jn 14:27) enjoys a great calm that is established in it, and the vine gives its fruit and the earth its increase and heaven its dew. The vine that gives its fruit is the spiritual contemplations in the truth... and the earth gives its increase, as the seed that Jesus cast into it bears thirty and sixty and a hundred (Mt 13:8, 23)... The earth presents its increase to him who sows it with tears and with sweat and sorrow, so he reaps it with joy (Ps 125:5)... "They that sow in tears shall reap in joy. He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him" (Ps 126:5). This abundant harvest is spiritual and concerns the divine word, as Hosea the prophet commanded: "Sow to yourselves in righteousness; reap according to goodness; plow for yourselves a plowing, for it is a time to seek the Lord until He come and teach you righteousness" (Hos 10:12)... As for heaven giving its dew, we shall understand the dew when we know the heaven that gives it. Heaven is no doubt none other than he who bears the image of the heavenly man (1 Cor 15:49), whose homeland is in heaven (Phil 3:20). For it was said of those who show forth the heavenly image of the Savior: "The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork" (Ps 18:1), and it was said of them in the great song in the Book of Deuteronomy: "Rejoice, O ye heavens, with him" (Deut 32:43), that is, rejoice with the Savior. How should they not rejoice and exult with Him when they have been formed in His image, as the Apostle says: "to be conformed to the image of his Son" (Rom 8:29), and also "we shall put on the image of the heavenly" (1 Cor 15:49)?! It is fitting for us to say that by their union in one heaven they give a heavenly dew, but each one gives his own dew, imitating Moses who said: "My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew" (Deut 32:2)].

8.7.2.en: Sixth: As the believer, by God's dwelling in his heart, comes to have these divine blessings, he becomes a heaven that gives its dew, for he is no longer a curse to others nor to himself, but is a blessing... This is what we speak of in the commentary on the end of this chapter [20-23].

8.8.0.en: 16 These are the things that ye shall do; Speak ye every man the truth to his neighbour; execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates: 17 And let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his neighbour; and love no false oath: for all these are things that I hate, saith the LORD.

8.8.1.en: Amid these blessings that come upon their lives by the Lord's dwelling in them, which seem as if impossible [9], He urges them to hold fast to the divine commandment so that they do not fall under His wrath like their fathers. "These are the things that ye shall do; Speak ye every man the truth to his neighbour; execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates: and let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his neighbour; and love no false oath: for all these are things that I hate, saith the LORD" [16-17].

8.8.2.en: Now that He is rebuilding the temple and renewing Jerusalem, His holy city, He wanted this work to be founded on truth joined to righteousness, or in other words to be based on practical truth in the lives of His children. And here we notice the following in these commandments of His:

8.8.3.en: First: He begins with our relationship with our brethren in the Lord, such as speaking with our brethren in truth, and judging with justice and peace, etc... and ends with a commandment concerning our relationship with Him, "a false oath," as if God wants our inner Jerusalem to be founded on true practical love with our brethren, yet in the Lord.

8.8.4.en: Second: He begins by speaking of "truth"; this is the foundation of true building. What is this truth with which we speak to our neighbors and by which we judge but the manifestation of the "Lord Christ" Himself in our speech as in our conduct, for He declared of Himself that He is "the truth." This truth is not preached by word only but is proclaimed with power through practical conduct in the lives of the shepherds as of the flock.

8.8.5.en: St. Didymus the Blind sees that the Lord begins His speech concerning the spiritual leaders, who must proclaim "the truth" not by theoretical intellectual knowledge alone but through a virtuous life and practical conduct. Among his words in commenting on this divine statement: [It is fitting for us to hear the words of Jesus and practice them, as He Himself declared: "Whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man" (Mt 7:24)].

8.8.6.en: [Let our deeds declare the spiritual teachings that we present; thus a man becomes "a workman that needeth not to be ashamed" (2 Tim 2:15). With this thought the Apostle writes to his disciple to keep purity, gravity, sincerity and sound speech that cannot be condemned (Tit 2:7-8). What is sound speech that cannot be condemned but practicing what we enjoin on others, and our pure fidelity to what we hold out to others concerning the faith?!].

8.8.7.en: Thus the Fathers of the Church affirmed the necessity of proclaiming the truth by practical life and its manifestation in daily conduct. Among the words of St. John Chrysostom: [He who governs others must be more radiant than any shining star; his life must be without blemish; all look to him and see in his life a model for themselves].

8.8.8.en: Third: He continues His speech, saying: "execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates"... If "truth" is the foundation on which the new city is built, then it is fitting that truth be mixed with peace. Heavenly truth opens the heart with love so that it is wide enough to bear with others, being at peace, if possible, with all men.

8.8.9.en: St. Didymus the Blind comments on His saying "in your gates," saying that the courts of justice founded on truth mixed with peace are at the gates, to sort those entering the city from those who are barred from it. It is as though peace does not mean flattery at the expense of truth or leniency toward evil, but while the heart is widened with love, nothing defiled or abominable must enter the holy city!

8.8.10.en: Let us love all and open our hearts to peace with all, but let us not open our inner gates to evil and sin out of courtesy to others!

8.8.11.en: Fourth: "let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his neighbour," meaning the inner forgetting of every wrong a neighbor has done to us, or not thinking ill of his actions. Joseph the Righteous presents to us a living example of this virtue; in his composure he realizes what his brothers did to him, but his heart sees beyond his brothers' actions: the hand of God working for his salvation and theirs; therefore with a wide heart he said to them: "God did send me before you to preserve life" (Gen 45:5) "But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive" (Gen 50:20).

8.8.12.en: When a man realizes the divine purposes his soul rests greatly in everything, and his heart is widened with peace for everyone, even for his opponents, so he does not resist evil with evil but with good and with love.

8.8.13.en: Fifth: Finally He asks them not to love a false oath, which the Lord hates, since He commanded us: "Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain" (Ex 20:7).

8.9.0.en: 18 And the word of the LORD of hosts came unto me, saying, 19 "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; The fast of the fourth month, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth, shall be to the house of Judah joy and gladness, and cheerful feasts; therefore love the truth and peace.

8.9.1.en: "The fast of the fourth month, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth, shall be to the house of Judah joy and gladness, and cheerful feasts; therefore love the truth and peace" [18-19].

8.9.2.en: Their past life had been marked by fasting with mourning because of the chastenings that came upon them for their sins; and now that the Lord dwells in their midst and declares His dwelling in them, He turns their hearts to joy and their life to an unceasing feast. So also the true Christian in the midst of his fasts and sufferings, as he realizes the indwelling of God in him, inner joy does not cease from him and the feast does not stop in his life.

8.9.3.en: In the previous chapter we spoke about fasting as not merely abstaining from food but stopping from evil together with enjoying the Lord Christ, the bread of life. This concerns spiritual fasting; as for the feast, St. Athanasius the Apostolic says: [Jesus Christ, who is the way and the door and everything for us, is also "our feast," as the blessed Paul says: "For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us" (1 Cor 5:7)]. And as fasting is not merely abstaining from foods, so the feast is not eating and drinking but a joyful life in the Lord. Pope Athanasius the Apostolic says: [Let us not keep the feast in an earthly manner but as those who keep a feast in heaven with the angels... Let us rejoice not in ourselves but in the Lord, so that we may be with the saints]. [Let us not stop at merely performing the rites of the feast but prepare to draw near to the divine Lamb and touch the heavenly food].

8.10.s.en: 5. Their dwelling a blessing for the nations:

8.10.0.en: 20 Thus saith the LORD of hosts; It shall yet come to pass, that there shall come people, and the inhabitants of many cities: 21 And the inhabitants of one city shall go to another, saying, Let us go speedily to pray before the LORD, and to seek the LORD of hosts: I will go also. 22 Yea, many people and strong nations shall come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem, and to pray before the LORD. 23 "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you."

8.10.1.en: God does not accept half measures: either one is a curse to himself as to others, or a blessing to himself as to his brethren, for He says: "And it shall come to pass, that as ye were a curse among the heathen, O house of Judah, and house of Israel; so will I save you, and ye shall be a blessing" [13]. And here He explains to them how they will be a blessing, saying: "Yea, many people and strong nations shall come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem, and to pray before the LORD... In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you" [22-23].

8.10.2.en: First: When God's wrath came upon them and the captivity took place, they became a curse among the nations; and the sign of this curse is the ruin of Jerusalem even in the days of the feast, as Jeremiah says lamenting Zion: "The ways of Zion do mourn, because none come to the solemn feasts: all her gates are desolate: her priests sigh" (Lam 1:4). And as St. Didymus the Blind says: [How should the ways of Zion not mourn, when no one comes to her and there is none to hasten in going up to Jerusalem to celebrate the feast and to assemble there...?!]. But now that she has turned from curse to blessing she has drawn many peoples to her so that they may enjoy the feast and rejoice in the Lord. Zechariah the prophet says: "Yea, many people and strong nations shall come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem." And since Jerusalem means "vision of peace," the sign of blessing is the drawing of many to enjoy this spiritual vision of reconciliation on the Cross and obtaining peace with God.

8.10.3.en: Second: St. Didymus the Blind comments on the saying: "I will go also." He says that the prophet, seeing crowds of peoples and nations coming from Jerusalem, had his heart set aflame with longing, and desired to be among those coming, declaring it by his saying: "I will go also." He also sees that the speaker here is the Savior, who declares His entrance into Jerusalem, leading these peoples in the spirit of victory, saying: "I have raised him up with victory, and I will make all his ways smooth; he shall build my city, and shall release my captives, not for price nor for reward, saith the LORD of hosts" (Isa 45:13). As He opens the door, the door of victory and triumph, and builds the inner holy city, and frees the soul from its captivity not by a material price or an earthly reward but by His precious blood, the peoples and nations seek the Lord and enter the new Jerusalem to entreat the Lord's favor, those of whom the Apostle said: "But ye are come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven" (Heb 12:22-23).

8.10.4.en: Third: The Lord does not say that He blesses them but what is greater: "ye shall be a blessing"; through them the nations are blessed, and in Zephaniah He says that they become "a praise among all the peoples of the earth" (Zeph 3:20), and in Micah they become "as a dew from the LORD" (Mic 5:7). So he who carries the Lord in his heart carries a blessing for others, and is a song of joy by which their hearts rejoice in the Lord; they become like the heavenly dew that quenches the flame of the world's destructive fire!

8.10.5.en: Fourth: He concludes His speech about the blessing with the fact that ten men from all languages of the nations take hold of the skirt of a Jewish man, saying, We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you. This is a picture of the bride who says in the Song: "Draw me, we will run after thee" (Song 1:4), for as she sets out toward her Bridegroom she carries with her ten persons whom she gains for the Lord by her holy life and her witness for the Lord. This from one side, and from another side we who were formerly of the Gentiles do not deny that we have received from them the Old Testament with what it contains of the Law and the prophecies as a way to the knowledge of salvation in Christ Jesus. We are indebted to them for receiving the faith in the Messiah the Savior.

8.10.6.en: St. Didymus the Blind sees that this Jew by whose skirt ten men from all the nations take hold is none other than the Lord Christ, who came forth from the tribe of Judah (Heb 7:14), as was said by Isaiah the prophet: "And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious" (Isa 11:10). He is the object of expectation not of one nation but of all the nations.

8.10.7.en: As for the number ten, it signifies, in the opinion of St. Didymus the Blind, the believers who have become ten virgins (Mt 25:1), having five holy senses of the body and five holy inner senses. As for these, since the believers bear the name "Jesus Christ," the beginning of His name is the letter "Iota," which is equivalent to the number 10 in the Greek language.
